feeds.title: Southern Exposure Seed Exchange
feeds.description: The blog covers Organic & Heirloom vegetable seeds, growing advice, seed saving, and more. Worker-owned seed company specializing in heirloom and organic seeds. We are particularly focused on the South Eastern United States, though we carry many varieties that will perform well in a wide range of climates.

feeds.title: Maryland Grows
feeds.description: We help Maryland residents grow! Learn timely tips to manage your lawn, ornamental plants, and food gardens, with advice from University of Maryland experts and certified horticulturists.

feeds.title: Central Texas Gardener Blog
feeds.description: Central Texas Gardener is all about organic gardening, outstanding water wise plants, design inspiration, wildlife, homegrown food, and creative fun in the garden. See how to tackle the techniques, pick drought-tough plants for wildlife, fill up your kitchen with fresh food, and enrich your soul with artistic designs and homegrown philosophy from hands-on gardeners.

feeds.title: The Dallas Garden School Blog
feeds.description: Learn to grow vegetables, flowers, annuals, and perennials that thrive in Zone 8. Education, information, and inspiration for gardening in North Texas.

feeds.title: Home Garden Joy
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Jeanne Grunert, master gardener, gardening book author, herbalist, and writer. If you're new to gardening, welcome! I make it simple and easy for you to grow a gorgeous garden and cook with the fresh vegetables, fruits, and herbs that you grow.

feeds.title: The Garden Diaries Blog
feeds.description: A garden/floral designer who has had a trowel in hand and dirty fingernails since I was four years old, I have over 30 years of hands-on experience. I am Claire - a writer, consultant, teacher, lecturer, beekeeper, and garden designer. I love to write about all my successes and failures (many of these!) in gardening.

feeds.title: Home & Garden Information Center Blog
feeds.description: We are here to answer questions on home and garden topics. The Clemson Extension Home & Garden Information Center (HGIC) delivers unbiased, research-based information to South Carolina residents.

feeds.title: Triangle Gardener Magazine
feeds.description: Triangle Gardener is North Carolina's leader in gardening news and information, including a print magazine, website, and a podcast - all about gardening!

feeds.title: Mary Snoddy Blog
feeds.description: Mary shares gardening hints for the Southeast US, how to grow trees, shrubs, flowers and bulbs.

feeds.title: South Florida Gardening
feeds.description: We are a small group of South Floridians who share a love of organic gardening, cooking, and leading a healthy lifestyle. We garden together in Miami on a weekly basis year-round and enjoy the labor, harvest, and feeling of community that this provides us.

feeds.title: Southern Meadows
feeds.description: I'm Karin, a gardener, photographer, and writer. Southern Meadows is a private habitat garden, located in Northeast Georgia's Piedmont, zone 8a. Our goal is to create a wildlife-friendly garden to support a wide variety of native birds, insects, arachnids, reptiles, and amphibians.

feeds.title: Austin Organic Gardeners Blog
feeds.description: Since 1945, our members have shared information about successfully raising vegetables and ornamentals without using harsh fertilizers and toxic pesticides that harm the soil and disturb the ecological balance. We are the oldest organic gardening club in the U.S. as recognized by Rodale Institute and in 2020 during the pandemic, we celebrated 75 years as a club.

feeds.title: Central Florida Gardening
feeds.description: Growing veggies, herbs and fruits in Zone 9.

feeds.title: The Citrus Guy
feeds.description: Darren Sheriff is a Certified Professional Nurseryman, Master Gardener and works at a nursery. He loves working with other gardeners and plant problem solving.

feeds.title: Grow Your Own Food Anywhere
feeds.description: We are all concerned with the quality and safety of our food today. You can grow on a back patio, on a windowsill, in a spare room, in your living room, on a balcony, in a greenhouse, just about anywhere that you can spare a little space. There are many space-saving methods and methods of growing that will increase your yield and your harvest. We intend to discuss all of these options on this blog.

feeds.title: Experiential Gardener Blog
feeds.description: My name is Rebecca and I started the Experiential Gardener channel to share practical how-to Texas gardening information and tips that I have found to be useful based on my experience gardening in North Central Texas Zone 8a over the last forty plus years.

feeds.title: Leek Garden
feeds.description: Hi! My name is Julia, and I want to share my experiences with, tips and tricks that I have learned from my time gardening. My passion for plants came out of necessity. With two kids and one full income, our family needed to find a way to make ends meet. A vegetable garden, small at best, seemed like the best place to start to stretch our grocery budget. Here you won't just find product reviews. While I might let you know my favourites, I want you to walk away with new knowledge each time.

feeds.title: Using Georgia Native Plants
feeds.description: I'm Ellen Honeycutt. I consider myself to be an average gardener with perhaps an above-average passion for it! Fostering an appreciation for native plants is now a passion of mine, and I love to help other people learn more about the benefits of native plants. I also like to help people figure out which plants might work best in their garden.

feeds.title: Southern Gardening Gal Blog
feeds.description: I'm Nikki, the Southern Gardening Gal. I grew up working in the garden. Helping people enjoy their yard, garden & home with simple, quick and usually cheap ideas is what I like to do. That hurdle seems much higher than it really is and I want to help people get started with that dream garden or just a potted plant!
